sections.h2: Where to take a deed in Berrien County
sections.html:
The office occupies the Berrien County Administration Center, 701 Main Street, St. Joseph, MI 49085. Staff are present on weekdays that are not county holidays, with doors open from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. The window for taking in documents is shorter, ending at 4:30 p.m., and the public search computers go dark at 4:45 p.m.

Questions go to 269-983-7111, extension 8562. Paper reaches this one counter from every city, village and township in the county, from Benton Harbor and New Buffalo to Niles and Three Oaks.

  • Deliver the original in person, by courier, or by USPS, UPS or FedEx to 701 Main Street.
  • Slip in a self addressed return envelope, since the recorded paper travels back to whoever you name on it.
  • Photocopies get turned away because the office only records originals with live signatures.
  • Pay the whole amount up front. Checks should name the Register of Deeds, because a check meant for another county department will bounce the whole packet back.

The county charges $30 for any document, however long, the flat Michigan charge per recordable event. Certification and transfer tax can be added when the paper is a deed.

The treasurer's certificate has to accompany a warranty deed, any deed with a warranty covenant, a land contract or its assignment, and a master deed for a condominium.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a Berrien County sale
sections.html:
Two taxes apply to a non exempt deed of $100 or more. The county levy is 55 cents for each $500 of the price and the state levy is $3.75 for each $500, and a leftover fraction counts as a whole block. Added up, that is $4.30 per block. The county posts a rate chart that turns sale prices into dollar amounts.

State the whole price on the deed or attach a real estate valuation affidavit. Name any exemption on the instrument itself. The purchase contract assigns who pays, so confirm with the title agent.

The two statutes differ on exemptions. MCL 207.526, the state act, excuses a gift of a home to a child or grandchild, court orders with no stated price, and a transfer made through a mortgage foreclosure. MCL 207.505, the county act, shares many exemptions but has no family transfer item, so settle which tax applies before anyone signs.

sections.h2: What a deed needs before staff will accept it
sections.html:
These items show up most with house sales and estates.

  • Bring a certified death certificate, sealed by the clerk, to record that a joint owner has died (MCL 565.48). Recording it does not change the earlier deed, which stays the most current deed of record until someone files a new one.
  • A court paper must show the court's certification and seal.
  • For a notary, try the County Clerk by appointment on the main number, extension 8233, or a bank, municipal office or title company, some of which charge a fee.
  • Employees do not write deeds for the public. Ask a lawyer or title insurer, or find a template online or in an office supply store.
  • Mortgage survey reports do not go on file here. Only a certified survey that was actually recorded appears in the index.

Every recorded paper turns into a public record, and any member of the public may buy a copy for $1 per page. Once a loan is repaid, the lender files a discharge of mortgage at this office, and a buyer's closer checks for it.

A short checklist before you leave home: the original deed with live signatures, an acknowledgment from a notary or court officer, payment in full on a check that names the Register of Deeds, and a self addressed return envelope. If a co-owner has died, bring the certified death certificate. If a court order moved the title, make sure it carries the court's certification and seal. Staff cannot fix a defective deed at the counter, so a rejected packet means another trip or another mailing.

The county website has a Land Records Search page for lookups and an e-Recording page for electronic filing. The property and taxes page also links to online Register of Deeds services, the transfer tax chart and a flowchart on splitting or combining parcels.

Ahead of a closing, search by name for the chain of title, open mortgages and recorded liens. Counter searches by staff run 50 cents per year covered. Owners who intend to hold back a piece of their lot should read the split and combine flowchart first, since that process runs through other offices.

An heir preparing to list should pull the earlier deed and any recorded death certificate before the listing goes live, so the title agent can tell exactly who holds the interest.

Keep the departments straight when you chase a payoff. The Register of Deeds is an elected office that reviews and records papers moving or burdening land. The County Treasurer is a separate elected office with a four year term, and the Equalization Department prepares the report that sets the equalized tax base for the Board of Commissioners.

Tax payoff questions belong with the treasurer, not the Register. In a normal sale the closing agent requests the payoff, collects the transfer tax and sends the deed for recording, so most sellers only sign. If you sell for cash and as-is, the recording steps are the same, but there is usually no lender appraisal to wait on.

For an estate sale, plan the order. First record the death certificate if a joint owner died, then record the new deed, then let the closing agent clear any mortgage discharge still pending. Each paper becomes a separate recording, and each recording carries its own $30 fee, so ask the title agent for a total before you write the check.

sections.h2: Berrien County housing at a glance
sections.html: The July 2025 population estimate is 152,444, which is 1.3 percent under the 2020 base. Housing stock totals 78,132 units and 63,999 households, and owner occupancy sits at 72.8 percent. The typical owned home was worth $224,300 over the 2020 to 2024 period. Monthly costs for owners paying a mortgage had a median of $1,462, and gross rent had a median of $942. Permits issued in 2025 numbered 372.

faqs.q: How much is the Berrien County recording fee?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars flat per recordable document, regardless of how many pages it has. When a paper assigns or discharges several instruments, each one past the first adds $3.

faqs.q: What are Berrien's transfer tax numbers?
faqs.a: The county tax is 55 cents per $500 and the state tax is $3.75 per $500, with each block rounded up. That adds to $4.30 per block, unless the deed is exempt.

faqs.q: Can I mail a deed to Berrien County?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the signed original to 701 Main Street, St. Joseph, MI 49085, along with complete payment and a return envelope that carries postage. A photocopy cannot be recorded.

faqs.q: What is the cutoff for recording in Berrien County?
faqs.a: Documents are taken until 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, even though the office itself stays open to 5:00 p.m. and the public search computers close at 4:45 p.m.

faqs.q: Does the Berrien County recording office offer a notary?
faqs.a: No. Book a notary at the County Clerk through 269-983-7111, extension 8233, or visit a bank, municipal office or title company. Some of them charge a fee.
